sourceManifest.useBoundary: Concept reference only; all student-facing wording is original. Financial content is educational and not individualized advice.

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: A monthly plan that assigns available money to needs, wants, and goals.
clues.hint: Think of the plan you make before deciding how to use your money.
clues.definition: A plan that estimates income and directs money toward expenses, saving, and other priorities.
clues.signal: The wording points to planning ahead and dividing limited money among several purposes.
clues.explanation: This term fits because it names a forward-looking money plan. Students can compare expected earnings with likely costs and decide what amount to reserve for each category before spending.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: Money received from work, a business, or another regular source.
clues.hint: It is the money coming in, before you decide where it will go.
clues.definition: Money that a person, household, or organization receives during a stated period.
clues.signal: The phrase received from work distinguishes money entering a situation from money being paid out.
clues.explanation: The answer is the general name for funds coming in. A paycheck is one example, but the concept can also include earnings from a small business or another source.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: A payment for something a person, household, or business uses.
clues.hint: Look for the word for money going out to cover a cost.
clues.definition: An amount of money spent or a cost incurred in obtaining goods, services, or operations.
clues.signal: A payment for something used describes an outflow, the opposite direction from earnings.
clues.explanation: This is correct because it labels a cost that must be paid. Rent, transportation, and supplies can each be recorded as this kind of item in a money plan.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: Money deliberately kept for a later purpose instead of used now.
clues.hint: It describes funds you reserve today for a future need or goal.
clues.definition: Money set aside from current use for future needs, goals, or emergencies.
clues.signal: The contrast between later and now identifies funds reserved rather than immediately spent.
clues.explanation: The answer fits because it refers to putting some money aside. Keeping a reserve can help prepare for a planned purchase or an unexpected need without making a specific financial recommendation.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: An amount charged or earned because money is borrowed or deposited over time.
clues.hint: This can be the price of using someone else's money for a while.
clues.definition: A charge paid by a borrower or an amount earned by a saver, usually stated as a rate.
clues.signal: Borrowed or deposited money over time signals the added amount connected to the use of funds.
clues.explanation: This term applies in both lending and saving situations. It can add to what a borrower repays, or it can be credited to money held in an account, depending on the arrangement.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: The original sum borrowed or invested, before added charges or earnings.
clues.hint: Focus on the starting amount, not the extra amount that may build over time.
clues.definition: The original amount of money in a loan or investment, excluding accumulated interest.
clues.signal: Original sum and before added amounts point to the base figure used in later calculations.
clues.explanation: The answer names the starting balance. In a loan, payments may reduce this amount while interest is calculated separately; in an investment, it is the initial money put to work.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: An arrangement that lets someone receive money or goods now and repay later.
clues.hint: It involves trust that a future payment will be made.
clues.definition: The ability or agreement to obtain money, goods, or services now with repayment due later.
clues.signal: Receive now and repay later describes a delayed-payment arrangement built on expected repayment.
clues.explanation: This is the right term because it describes access before full payment. The arrangement may involve money directly or the purchase of goods and services with a future obligation.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: Money or value that one party is obligated to repay to another.
clues.hint: This is the obligation left after receiving money or value to be repaid.
clues.definition: An obligation to repay money or another agreed value to a lender or other party.
clues.signal: Obligated to repay directs attention to what is owed rather than the agreement that provided it.
clues.explanation: The answer identifies the unpaid obligation itself. It can result from borrowing, buying with delayed payment, or another arrangement in which repayment is required.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: Funds provided under an agreement that they will be paid back later.
clues.hint: Think of the money supplied at the beginning of a borrowing arrangement.
clues.definition: Money or property given by one party to another with an agreement for later repayment.
clues.signal: Provided under an agreement for later repayment identifies the transaction that creates an obligation.
clues.explanation: This word fits the transaction in which funds are supplied with repayment terms. It differs from the unpaid balance, which is the obligation that remains after receiving the funds.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: A required payment collected by government to help fund public services.
clues.hint: It is a compulsory payment connected with government services and programs.
clues.definition: A compulsory payment imposed by a government to raise revenue for public purposes.
clues.signal: Required payment and public services distinguish a government levy from a voluntary purchase.
clues.explanation: The answer is a general civic and financial term for a mandatory government charge. Collected funds can support shared public functions, with rules varying by jurisdiction and type of payment.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: A broad rise in prices that can reduce what each unit of money buys.
clues.hint: Think about a general pattern where the same amount purchases fewer items.
clues.definition: A sustained increase in the overall price level that lowers the purchasing power of money.
clues.signal: Broad rise and reduced buying power describe an economy-wide price pattern rather than one product becoming costly.
clues.explanation: This concept fits because it concerns overall price levels, not just a single store or item. When prices rise broadly, a fixed amount of money may obtain fewer goods or services.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: Money or resources committed with the expectation of a future return or benefit.
clues.hint: It involves putting resources to work for a possible later result.
clues.definition: The commitment of money, time, or resources in expectation of future income, growth, or benefit.
clues.signal: Committed now for a future return signals a choice made with an expected later outcome.
clues.explanation: The answer covers a resource commitment intended to produce a later benefit. Outcomes can vary, so the clue teaches the general concept without suggesting a personal financial choice.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: Something owned that has value or could provide a future benefit.
clues.hint: It names a valuable thing an individual or organization controls.
clues.definition: A resource owned or controlled that has economic value or potential future benefit.
clues.signal: Owned value and future benefit identify a resource on the positive side of a balance picture.
clues.explanation: This term fits a valuable resource, such as cash, equipment, or property. What matters is that it is controlled and has value, rather than that it represents an amount owed.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: A financial obligation that an individual or organization must settle.
clues.hint: In an accounting picture, it is the side representing obligations to others.
clues.definition: A debt or other present obligation that requires payment or settlement in the future.
clues.signal: Must settle emphasizes a recorded obligation, especially when contrasted with owned resources.
clues.explanation: The answer is an accounting word for an obligation. It includes amounts owed and is commonly considered alongside resources owned when describing an organization’s financial position.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: The amount left when a business brings in more than it spends.
clues.hint: It is the positive remainder after the costs are subtracted from money earned.
clues.definition: The financial gain remaining when revenue exceeds the costs of operating or producing.
clues.signal: Amount left after spending identifies a positive remainder rather than total money collected.
clues.explanation: This word names the surplus after costs have been accounted for. It is different from total sales money because it considers what was spent to run the activity or provide the product.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: Total money a business receives from its usual sales or services before costs are removed.
clues.hint: This is the incoming total from business activity before subtracting operating costs.
clues.definition: The total income generated by a business from normal operations before expenses are deducted.
clues.signal: Before costs are removed identifies a gross incoming amount instead of the remainder after expenses.
clues.explanation: The answer is the money generated through normal business activity before expenses are subtracted. Comparing that incoming total with costs can help explain whether the business has a gain or loss.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: The money or resources required to make, buy, or provide something.
clues.hint: It is what must be given up or paid to obtain or produce something.
clues.definition: The amount of money, effort, or other resources required to acquire, produce, or maintain something.
clues.signal: Required to make or obtain points to the sacrifice or payment associated with a choice.
clues.explanation: This term fits the resources needed for an item or activity. A business may track this amount when making a product, while a household may consider it before choosing a purchase.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: The condition in which limited resources cannot satisfy every possible want.
clues.hint: It explains why people and communities must make choices among competing wants.
clues.definition: The economic condition in which available resources are insufficient to meet all human wants.
clues.signal: Limited resources and every possible want signal the basic economic problem of unavoidable choice.
clues.explanation: The answer describes why choices are necessary. Time, labor, land, and materials are finite, while people can imagine many uses for them, so priorities must be set.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: The willingness and ability of buyers to purchase a good or service at a given price.
clues.hint: In economics, wanting an item matters along with being able to buy it.
clues.definition: The quantity of a good or service that consumers are willing and able to buy at various prices.
clues.signal: Willingness plus ability to purchase identifies the buyer side of a market relationship.
clues.explanation: This term is more specific than simply wanting something. In market analysis, it concerns how much buyers can and will purchase at particular prices, which may change as conditions change.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: financial-literacy
clues.clue: The amount of a good or service that sellers are willing to offer at a given price.
clues.hint: In a market, this describes the seller side rather than the buyer side.
clues.definition: The quantity of a good or service that producers are willing and able to offer for sale at various prices.
clues.signal: Sellers willing to offer identifies the producer side of the market relationship.
clues.explanation: The answer concerns what producers can and will offer for sale. It is paired with buyer interest when classes explore how markets coordinate available goods and services.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: The long-term pattern of temperature, precipitation, and other conditions in a region.
clues.hint: Think of patterns measured across many years, not this afternoon's conditions.
clues.definition: The long-term average pattern and range of atmospheric conditions in a particular place or region.
clues.signal: Long-term pattern and region distinguish a broad record from conditions on one day.
clues.explanation: This is the term for patterns observed over long periods. Scientists describe it with averages and variation in factors such as temperature, rainfall, wind, and seasonal cycles.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: The current atmospheric conditions, such as rain, wind, cloud cover, and temperature.
clues.hint: It describes what the sky and air are doing now or over a short time.
clues.definition: The state of the atmosphere at a specific time and place, including temperature, wind, and precipitation.
clues.signal: Current conditions and short time point to an immediate atmospheric state rather than a long record.
clues.explanation: The answer fits day-to-day atmospheric conditions. A forecast can describe it for the next few hours or days, while long-running averages belong to a different environmental concept.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: A chemical element found in living things and in a common atmospheric compound.
clues.hint: This element is a building block of life and appears in several gases and fuels.
clues.definition: A nonmetal chemical element that forms the basis of organic compounds and occurs in many natural materials.
clues.signal: Living things and a familiar atmospheric compound point to an element, not to the compound itself.
clues.explanation: The answer is an element with an important role in biological molecules and Earth systems. It moves among air, water, rocks, soils, and living organisms through several natural processes.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: The release of a substance, energy, or radiation from a source into its surroundings.
clues.hint: It refers to something being sent out from a source, often into the air.
clues.definition: The act or process of releasing a substance, energy, or radiation from a source into the environment.
clues.signal: Release from a source identifies an outward flow rather than a substance already present.
clues.explanation: This word describes the process of sending something outward. It can apply to gases, light, heat, sound, or particles, so the term is broader than any one specific substance.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: Able to be naturally replenished on a humanly useful timescale.
clues.hint: It describes a resource that nature can replace relatively quickly.
clues.definition: Capable of being replenished naturally at a rate that can support continued use over time.
clues.signal: Naturally replenished and useful timescale point to how quickly a resource can be replaced.
clues.explanation: The answer describes a resource category based on renewal. Whether a particular use remains sustainable can still depend on the rate of use and local conditions.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: The careful protection and wise use of natural resources and ecosystems.
clues.hint: It focuses on safeguarding nature while using resources thoughtfully.
clues.definition: The protection, management, and careful use of natural resources, species, and ecosystems.
clues.signal: Protection joined with wise use signals stewardship rather than leaving every place entirely untouched.
clues.explanation: This term describes practices that seek to maintain natural systems and resources. It can include protecting habitats, reducing waste, restoring areas, and managing use with future conditions in mind.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: The variety of living organisms, including differences among species, genes, and ecosystems.
clues.hint: Think of the many forms of life in an area, from genes to whole ecosystems.
clues.definition: The variety and variability of life at genetic, species, and ecosystem levels.
clues.signal: Several levels of living variety indicate a scientific term broader than merely counting species.
clues.explanation: The answer names biological variety at more than one scale. A forest can have many species, genetic variation within each species, and different connected habitats, all contributing to this idea.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: The place and conditions where an organism normally lives and finds what it needs.
clues.hint: It is an organism's living place, including food, water, shelter, and space.
clues.definition: The natural environment in which an organism lives and obtains the resources needed to survive.
clues.signal: A place providing living needs points to an ecological home rather than a species itself.
clues.explanation: This term includes more than a location on a map. It combines physical conditions and resources that allow an organism to find food, water, shelter, space, and suitable conditions.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: The introduction of harmful substances or forms of energy into air, water, or land.
clues.hint: It concerns contamination that can damage environmental quality or living things.
clues.definition: The presence or introduction of substances or energy that harms environmental quality or organisms.
clues.signal: Harmful introduction into air, water, or land identifies environmental contamination across several media.
clues.explanation: The answer is the general term for damaging contamination. It can involve chemicals, waste, particles, noise, heat, or light when those additions harm environmental conditions or organisms.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: Collecting and processing used materials so they can become new products or materials.
clues.hint: It gives discarded materials another useful turn through collection and processing.
clues.definition: The collection, sorting, and processing of used materials for conversion into new usable materials or products.
clues.signal: Used materials becoming new products identifies a recovery process rather than simply throwing less away.
clues.explanation: This word fits the system that recovers certain discarded materials for further use. Success depends on local collection rules, material quality, sorting, and available processing facilities.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: A nutrient-rich material formed when organic scraps decompose under managed conditions.
clues.hint: It is made when food scraps and yard materials break down into a soil-like amendment.
clues.definition: Decomposed organic material, often made from food and yard waste, used to improve soil.
clues.signal: Organic scraps breaking down into a soil amendment identify the product of managed decomposition.
clues.explanation: The answer is the finished material created as certain organic matter decomposes. It can return nutrients and organic matter to soil when produced and used appropriately.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: An extended period of unusually low precipitation that creates a water shortage.
clues.hint: It is more than a dry day; it is a prolonged lack of expected moisture.
clues.definition: A prolonged period of abnormally low precipitation that results in water shortages.
clues.signal: Extended low precipitation with a shortage separates a long hydrologic condition from ordinary sunny weather.
clues.explanation: This term describes a sustained lack of expected precipitation and available water. Its effects can differ by region and may influence agriculture, ecosystems, water supplies, and wildfire conditions.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: The wearing away and movement of rock or soil by water, wind, ice, or gravity.
clues.hint: It involves Earth material being carried away, not merely broken into smaller pieces.
clues.definition: The process by which rock or soil is worn away and transported by natural agents such as water or wind.
clues.signal: Wearing away plus movement identifies transport, which is the key distinction from simple breakdown.
clues.explanation: The answer includes both removal and transport of Earth material. Flowing water, wind, ice, and gravity can move sediment from one place and eventually deposit it somewhere else.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: An area of land where precipitation and runoff drain to the same stream, lake, or other outlet.
clues.hint: Trace rainwater downhill: the land area feeding one common outlet has this name.
clues.definition: A land area that collects precipitation and drains it to a common body of water or outlet.
clues.signal: Land draining to one outlet points to a geographic drainage area rather than the waterway itself.
clues.explanation: The answer identifies the land area connected by water flow to a shared outlet. Its boundaries often follow higher ground, and actions upstream can influence water conditions farther downstream.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: An underground layer of permeable rock or sediment that stores and transmits groundwater.
clues.hint: It is a below-ground formation through which water can be stored and move.
clues.definition: A body of permeable rock, sediment, or soil that contains and can yield groundwater.
clues.signal: Underground permeable layer and groundwater identify a geologic storage-and-flow formation.
clues.explanation: This term describes a subsurface formation with connected spaces that hold and transmit water. Wells may draw from such formations, whose recharge and quality depend on local geology and conditions.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: The large-scale clearing or conversion of forested land to another use.
clues.hint: It describes removing forest cover across a broad area, often changing the land's use.
clues.definition: The extensive removal of forest cover, commonly resulting in conversion of land to nonforest uses.
clues.signal: Large-scale clearing and land conversion distinguish this process from pruning or a single fallen tree.
clues.explanation: The answer refers to extensive loss of forest cover. Such change can alter habitat, soil, water movement, and local conditions; the effects depend on the place, scale, and subsequent land use.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: Meeting present needs while maintaining the conditions and resources future generations will need.
clues.hint: It asks whether today's choices can continue without undermining tomorrow's options.
clues.definition: The capacity to meet current needs while preserving environmental, social, and economic conditions for the future.
clues.signal: Present needs paired with future conditions signals a long-term balance among continuing needs.
clues.explanation: This term evaluates whether a practice can endure over time. It requires considering how current choices affect resources, ecosystems, communities, and opportunities available to later generations.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: Relating to heat from within Earth that can be used for heating or generating electricity.
clues.hint: Break it into Earth plus heat to identify an energy source beneath the surface.
clues.definition: Relating to the natural heat stored within Earth, especially when used as an energy source.
clues.signal: Heat from within Earth identifies an underground thermal source rather than sunlight or moving air.
clues.explanation: The answer describes energy associated with Earth’s internal heat. In suitable locations, hot water, steam, or ground temperatures can be used in systems for heating or electricity generation.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: Relating to the Sun or to energy captured from its light and heat.
clues.hint: This adjective describes systems powered by sunlight.
clues.definition: Of, relating to, or produced by the Sun, especially energy derived from sunlight.
clues.signal: Sunlight and heat point to an adjective for energy originating with the Sun.
clues.explanation: The answer modifies technologies and processes connected with the Sun. Panels can convert light into electricity, while other systems use sunlight’s heat for useful purposes.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker

clues.subject: environmental-literacy
clues.clue: A material, source of energy, or feature of nature that people can use to meet needs.
clues.hint: It is something useful that people draw on, such as water, soil, energy, or minerals.
clues.definition: A natural material, energy source, or environmental feature that can be used to support human needs.
clues.signal: Useful materials and energy sources point to the broad category of things people rely upon.
clues.explanation: This term covers many useful parts of the natural world, including water, forests, soil, minerals, and sunlight. Different resources renew at different rates and require careful management.
clues.sourceLicense: common-knowledge and Princeton WordNet reference marker
